H-OS-L1.name: Pebble
H-OS-L1.sphere: Strongest HEALING performer with n=95, mean=7.15 (±1.78), confidence=strong. Only 29 qualitative responses but 22/29 report improvement. Settle: 11 at 10 minutes, 7 at 5 minutes. Music: 10 Liked, 9 Loved. AutoGluon predicts 6.86 with cross-bucket routing to X-ME-L1 — slight overperformance. YouTube reach highest in HEALING (views=30) but still low absolute.
H-OS-L1.sphere_plain: One of the top performers for over-stimulation, helping two-thirds of users feel better. Particularly useful for caregivers supporting others through distress episodes. Most users found it calming within 10 minutes.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall
H-OS-L2.sphere: n=51, mean=6.92 (±1.73), confidence=strong. 16/21 qualitative improve. Settle time favors 10 minutes (10 responses). Music opinion divided (10 Liked, 6 Neutral, 5 Loved). AutoGluon does not prioritize OS-L2. Minimal YouTube views (5).
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Most users improve but opinions on the music are mixed — some find it just okay while others appreciate the sound. Takes around 10 minutes to settle. Works well but doesn't stand out emotionally.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier
H-OS-L3.sphere: n=47, mean=7.04 (±1.68), confidence=meaningful. 18/23 improve. Settle: 7 at 5 minutes, 5 at 10 minutes. Music: 11 Liked, 5 Neutral. Notably, 8/23 activity = Trying to sleep — strong sleep-adjacent utility. Minimal YouTube views (8). Panel divided on whether L3 offers sufficient differentiation from L1.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Good two-thirds success rate for calming from overstimulation, especially helpful when used before sleep. The rhythm feels balanced and not too active, which users appreciate.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow
H-AX-L1.sphere: HEALING anxiety leadership protocol with n=67, mean=7.22 (±1.93), confidence=strong. Qualitative data shows 18/23 respondents reporting Moderate-to-Significant improvement with 10-minute settle time (9 responses). AutoGluon predicts 7.84 for anxiety zone and cross-routes to Motivation (7.88) — suggests broader utility potential. YouTube reach minimal (views=7) despite strong outcomes — undiscovered efficacy signal.
H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: This anxiety protocol works well for most people, with many reporting they felt noticeably calmer within 10 minutes. The rhythm feels balancing and most listeners would recommend it to others dealing with stress.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage
H-AX-L2.sphere: n=48, mean=6.94 (±1.62), confidence=meaningful. Listener mix shows 60% self-listening, 30% clinical. 12/20 qualitative responses report Noticeable-to-Moderate improvement. Settle time clustered at 5-10 minutes. AutoGluon does not favor L2 over L1 for anxiety routing — L1 remains recommended tier. Very low YouTube reach (views=6).
H-AX-L2.sphere_plain: A solid anxiety resource that helps about two-thirds of users feel better. Some find it just okay while others really appreciate the calming effect. Works best for people using it during daily activities like commuting.

H-AX-L3.name: Valley
H-AX-L3.sphere: n=36, mean=7.08 (±1.89), confidence=meaningful. 15/20 qualitative responses report improvement but 4 report no effect. Settle times split between 10 minutes (10) and full session (4) — indicates entrainment variability. Rhythm opinion favorable (10 Very settling). Very low YouTube reach (views=4).

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor

AutoGluon prefers H-CR-L2 (7.96) for crisis routing — L2 may be more effective intervention.
H-CR-L1.sphere_plain: Intended for crisis moments, this helps about half of users shift out of extreme distress. Works fairly quickly for most people. Not a miracle solution but provides real support when things feel overwhelming.

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor

H-CR-L2.sphere_plain: A gentle but effective crisis intervention that most listeners find helpful within 10 minutes. Some really love the sound while others are neutral, but the outcome data shows real benefit.

H-CR-L3.name: Horizon

H-SL-L1.name: Lantern

T-FC-L3.name: Summit

sphere_commentary.overview:
The three series show distinct efficacy profiles where HEALING leads in mean outcomes (6.98) with low variance, THRIVING maintains comparable scores (6.96) with peak performance in Focus protocols, and TRANSFORMING exhibits expected higher spread (6.59) due to its ascending-arc design.
• HEALING (n=574) shows strongest consistency with DESCENT protocols performing reliably across anxiety, crisis and sleep zones
• THRIVING (n=245) achieves highest single-protocol score (T-FC-L3: 7.63) but Creative Flow subseries underperforms Focus & Clarity
• TRANSFORMING (n=181) aligns with design intent for low-affect states but shows bimodal risk in Mood & Energy protocols
• AutoGluon feature importance (avg_view_percentage: 0.277) signals retention metrics will become primary efficacy predictors as data grows
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The series follow expected design trajectories but reveal actionable cross-protocol opportunities.
• HEALING: DESCENT architecture produces reliable outcomes (mean 6.98) with all 12 protocols showing >52% positive responses; crisis protocols appropriately show lowest scores (53-55%) given acute listener states
• THRIVING: HOLD protocols peak in Focus & Clarity (T-FC-L3: 7.63, 71% positive) but Creative Flow series averages only 6.94 — suggesting potential entrainment barrier in flow-state induction designs
• TRANSFORMING: ASCENT protocols show 43-62% positive ratings with Motivation & Drive underperforming (X-MD-L1: 45%) despite AutoGluon predicting 7.88 for this zone — indicating entrainment failure requiring investigation
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Three protocols deviate significantly from expected patterns and warrant investigation.
• X-MC-L3: Lowest observed score in the entire dataset (mean=5.70, n=10, std=2.45) with 50% positive only — structural underperformance relative to L1/L2 variants
• T-FC-L3: Top THRIVING performer (mean=7.63, n=35) shows high drift (sim=0.53) suggesting analytical instability — may indicate evolving listener perception
• X-ME-L1: AutoGluon predicts highest efficacy (8.23) but observed mean=6.74 — 1.5 point underdelivery suggests entrainment barrier in ASCENT designs for Mood & Energy
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Multiple analyzers identified convergent development opportunities.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 (n=10): Lowest mean in dataset with high std — increase hold phase to support longer entrainment before outcome measurement
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-SL-L1: Strong performer (n=54, mean=7.19) but very low YouTube views (4) — investigate discovery barriers and visibility optimization
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC series: L3 significantly outperforms L1 despite same duration/Hz — create L2 variant that bridges the entrainment gap
• X-ME-L1 (n=39): Model predicts 8.23 but observes 6.74 — adjust ASCENT arc parameters to improve efficacy delivery
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Embedding analysis shows notable drift but insufficient clustering data for semantic pattern extraction.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: Protocols with sim<0.85 (X-MD-L3: 0.507, H-SL-L1: 0.530, T-FC-L3: 0.532) indicate evolving data patterns — validate whether true instability or signal evolution
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Cluster analysis disabled — requires >30 protocols with embeddings for stable grouping
• Embedding density remains LOW — interpret drift signals as directional only, not definitive

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: This anxiety protocol works well for most people, with many reporting they felt noticeably calmer within 10 minutes. The rhythm feels balancing and most listeners would recommend it to others dealing with stress.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: A solid anxiety resource that helps about two-thirds of users feel better. Some find it just okay while others really appreciate the calming effect. Works best for people using it during daily activities like commuting.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Helps many people feel calmer but takes longer than other options — about half the time users need the full session to feel the effect. Some people don't feel any change at all, unfortunately.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Intended for crisis moments, this helps about half of users shift out of extreme distress. Works fairly quickly for most people. Not a miracle solution but provides real support when things feel overwhelming.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: A gentle but effective crisis intervention that most listeners find helpful within 10 minutes. Some really love the sound while others are neutral, but the outcome data shows real benefit.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Works fastest when needed — several users report settling within the first couple minutes. Helps the majority feel better from extreme states, though not everyone connects with the music style.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: One of the top performers for over-stimulation, helping two-thirds of users feel better. Particularly useful for caregivers supporting others through distress episodes. Most users found it calming within 10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Most users improve but opinions on the music are mixed — some find it just okay while others appreciate the sound. Takes around 10 minutes to settle. Works well but doesn't stand out emotionally.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Good two-thirds success rate for calming from overstimulation, especially helpful when used before sleep. The rhythm feels balanced and not too active, which users appreciate.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Strong sleep-supporting protocol with fast results for most people. Many users fall asleep quickly after starting it. Some analytical instability detected across runs, so we're monitoring this one carefully.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Mixed results — some people get great sleep support while others find the rhythm too active. About two-thirds improve. Works best when used in therapeutic contexts with guidance.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Most users benefit, especially in quiet settings, but a few struggle to settle completely. Mixed opinions on the music but the rhythm generally feels balanced.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Mild creative support for about half of users. Takes a bit to kick in. Not super engaging for some — works best as background support rather than active creative catalyst.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Better than L1, with most users reporting improvement. Takes about 10 minutes to feel the effect. People who stick with it often feel a shift in creative energy.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Best in the Creative Flow series, helping about two-thirds of users. Mixed opinions on the music but the rhythm does its job. Takes 5-10 minutes to settle in.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Helps many focus but some find the rhythm slightly too busy. Good for about half of users. Works best when there's no competing background noise.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Calm focus aid with about two-thirds reporting improvement. Not universally loved but the people who need it tend to benefit. Settles within 10 minutes.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: The star of the Focus series — most users feel sharper and more focused after listening. Ideal for deep work sessions. Slower to settle (10 minutes) but the effect is strong.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Grounding support that works for most but takes time — almost half the users need 20 minutes to feel the effect. Good for daily maintenance but not for quick balance restoration.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Mixed results with higher variance — some feel balanced, others feel slightly distracted. Works best in low-demand situations. About 60% would recommend.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Controversial — several users (4 out of 19) said they never settled. May need adjustments for consistent entry. Those who benefit though find good emotional balance.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: About half of users experience mental clarity improvement. The music gets high marks but sometimes the effect doesn't match the quality. Works in calm environments.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Better clarity support than L1, with 60% experiencing benefit. Fast-acting for most. The rhythm gets strong praise. Good potential if promoted more effectively.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: The lowest performer — not recommended. Less than half users improve, and many find the rhythm too busy. Would benefit from significant redesign.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Helps motivation for less than half of users. Works quickly when it works. The low YouTube presence means many who might benefit haven't discovered it yet.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Mixed results — about half feel more motivated, but takes 20 minutes for some. The music is loved though, so there's potential with protocol adjustments.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: The surprise performer despite low sample size. Higher average than siblings suggests it might work for specific situations or populations not yet identified.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Core energy protocol with mixed results — about half improve but takes 20 minutes for some. The music is well-received and the model predicts high potential, suggesting untapped efficacy.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Stable performer with two-thirds improving. Interestingly, some feel the effect immediately while others take 20 minutes — individual variation is high.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Dip in performance at L3 — only 60% improve and some report no effect. The earlier versions (L1, L2) appear more effective than the highest tier.
